Convert 3D polygons to an envelope on a grid

Source: R/vector3d_to_envelope.R
vector3d_to_envelope.Rd

Puts SpatVector3D polygons onto the grid of template as a SpatEnvelope, as vect_to_envelope() does for 2D polygons with one depth range. Each cell a polygon touches gets that polygon's depth range. Cells that no polygon touches are NA, and so are cells where depth_min equals depth_max, which have no thickness.

Usage

vector3d_to_envelope(x, template)

Arguments

x

A SpatVector3D of polygons, from as_vector3d() or buffer_3d().

template

A SpatRaster whose grid (extent, resolution and CRS) the envelope uses; its values are ignored. For example, a SpatVoxel or a raster from create_study_raster(). Polygons are projected to its CRS if it isn't WGS84. Longitudes from 0 to 360 work too.

Value

A SpatEnvelope on the grid of template. Stops with an error if it would have no cells: when the polygons don't overlap template, or none of them has depth_max deeper than depth_min.

Details

Where polygons overlap, a cell gets the shallowest depth_min and the deepest depth_max of the polygons that cover it. An envelope has one depth range per cell, so polygons from 0 to 50 m and from 200 to 300 m over the same cell give 0 to 300 m there.

An envelope has no time, so the polygons' time intervals are dropped, with a message when any polygon has one. To make an envelope for one period, keep only the polygons for that period first.

See also

vect_to_envelope() for 2D polygons, as_envelope()

Examples

template <- terra::rast(nrows = 4, ncols = 4, xmin = 150, xmax = 154,
                        ymin = -24, ymax = -20, crs = "EPSG:4326")
square <- function(x0, y0) {
  sf::st_polygon(list(rbind(c(x0, y0), c(x0 + 2, y0), c(x0 + 2, y0 + 2),
                            c(x0, y0 + 2), c(x0, y0))))
}
areas <- sf::st_sf(
  top = c(0, 200), bottom = c(50, 300),
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(square(151, -23), square(152, -24), crs = 4326)
)
polygons <- as_vector3d(areas, depth_min = "top", depth_max = "bottom")

# The overlapping cell gets 0 to 300 m.
e <- vector3d_to_envelope(polygons, template)
terra::values(e)
#>       depth_min depth_max
#>  [1,]        NA        NA
#>  [2,]        NA        NA
#>  [3,]        NA        NA
#>  [4,]        NA        NA
#>  [5,]        NA        NA
#>  [6,]         0        50
#>  [7,]         0        50
#>  [8,]        NA        NA
#>  [9,]        NA        NA
#> [10,]         0        50
#> [11,]         0       300
#> [12,]       200       300
#> [13,]        NA        NA
#> [14,]        NA        NA
#> [15,]       200       300
#> [16,]       200       300
